races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
BOYLE Sports 'Pick Your Place' Handicap

runners_data.name: Invincible Will
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Gavin Cromwell who has solid recent 7f form on Good ground (won last time out at this trip and going), apprentice Jack Kearney claims 3lb which aids the weight, and hood headgear noted; the lack of a truly fierce pace is the key risk to a horse who needs to be delivered late.

runners_data.name: Time Bender
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good ground last time out and has placed at this level before, but a 264-day absence is a significant query on fitness; if William Durkan has this horse spot-on after a long break, the 7f trip and going suit well.

runners_data.name: Zenford
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for J P Murtagh with a consistent placed record at 7f, and Ben Coen takes the ride; sim-going figures are modest (0 wins from 5 on comparable ground) but he dictates here and the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that he is mapped slightly out of his natural lead role — he is absolutely the lead horse and that is his element.

runners_data.name: Dawn Romance
runners_data.note: Placed 1W3P on similar going but all best form has come at 5-6f, and this 7f trip on Good to Firm represents a significant stamina test given that breeding and form profile; the 61-day absence adds a fitness caveat, and the visor headgear is retained.

runners_data.name: Mighty Danu
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for Cromwell with a win over 7f on Good ground to his name but both recent runs have been disappointing (6th and 7th), and 58 days off adds an element of doubt; the trip suits if the pace develops into something more pressured.

runners_data.name: Dark Leader
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who ran second over 7f on Good ground last time, making him one of the most course-and-distance relevant horses in the field at this going; placed record here is promising but Andrew Slattery has not had a big-race win in 14 days and the trainer's 2/7 T14 is modest.

runners_data.name: Venetian Star
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose recent form shows three placed finishes at 7-8f, but has been pushed forward on the map due to field congestion — Luke McAteer will need to find cover from a wide draw and this horse is not ideally suited to making up ground on quick, flat ground; STYLE_FIT flag applies.

runners_data.name: Caitouna
runners_data.note: Won last time over 7f on Good ground and Dylan Browne McMonagle is likely to seek a forward position despite the redistribution flag — a natural prominent racer whose trainer Paul Flynn has a quiet T14 (0/13), but the recent win at this course and trip combination makes the form highly relevant regardless of tactical positioning.

runners_data.name: Watch Tower
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for G M Lyons and Colin Keane who has a useful placed record at 7f (0W but multiple placed) and handles both Good and Standard; no win on record but consistent, and Keane's ability to position him ideally off the pace makes this horse one to track in running.

runners_data.name: Chapel Lane
runners_data.note: Uncertain style (tagged U) for W McCreery and Wayne Lordan, with a mixed form string including placed efforts at 7-8f on Good; visor headgear noted and all five recent runs have come on Good ground at Leopardstown which is a positive, though no wins from those five visits raises a concern about a decisive turn of foot.

races.paceDynamic: Zenford is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to challenge for the lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front on Good to Firm ground over 7f at Leopardstown. Behind him, Dark Leader and Watch Tower are the most natural prominent types likely to track in second and third, creating a measured pace that will not burn off hold-up horses early but equally will not collapse into a sprint finish. The field carries more pace than the map can accommodate — Caitouna and Venetian Star are both genuine prominent and hold-up types respectively who have been pushed back on the map, with Caitouna the more likely of the two to press for a forward position given Dylan Browne McMonagle's aggressive riding style, while Venetian Star will likely be consigned to the rear. This race shape — a single front-runner controlling an honest but not breakneck gallop on quick ground — strongly favours horses that can travel prominently in behind the leader and produce a sustained finishing effort, rewarding the patient but positionally savvy closer over the pure hold-up horse who needs a truly taxing pace to set them up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zenford Controls, Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Zenford dictates an honest, uncontested gallop and the field fans out turning in for a sustained 2f duel.
scenarios.body: Zenford's rhythm sets the tempo just fast enough to stretch hold-up horses but not so fierce that he ties himself up, and horses travelling fluidly in behind — particularly those with 7f form on good ground — can produce a clean run to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Leader or Watch Tower track Zenford closely and Zenford fades inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The pace genuinely collapses in the straight as Zenford is overhauled, and the horse sitting second or third into the final 2f inherits the advantage before hold-up horses can pick up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Zenford Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is modest enough that Zenford conserves energy and quickens again inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: On Good to Firm ground with no pressure, Zenford's front-running profile allows him to control the tempo and exploit a lack of sustained finishing pace from behind, proving hard to reel in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop proves deceptively fast and the field spreads wide, opening a clear late lane for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Though Invincible Will and Mighty Danu are genuine hold-up horses, this scenario is discounted because Venetian Star — another potential closer — is not racing in its natural role, and the pace is unlikely to be fierce enough to fully set up a late surge.

watchPoints.text: Zenford (Ben Coen) faces no front-running rival in this field — watch whether he is allowed to stride clear unchallenged from the gates, as an uncontested lead on Good to Firm could prove very hard to peg back.

Caitouna (Dylan Browne McMonagle) is mapped to midfield but is a natural prominent racer — watch the first furlong to see whether McMonagle pushes forward aggressively, which would change the race shape by adding pressure to Zenford earlier than expected.

Time Bender returns from a 264-day absence — watch the market move closely as any significant support would suggest William Durkan has the horse at peak fitness, which would make its Good-ground 7f win look very relevant.

Invincible Will carries hood headgear and Jack Kearney (3lb claim) — watch how far back Kearney settles him early, as a hold-up horse in a moderately-paced race needs to be in a position to sustain a run from 2f out, not launch from last.

Watch Tower (Colin Keane) has a strong placed record over 7f but has not yet won — watch whether Keane places him closer than usual to exploit the pace set by Zenford, as a prominent position off the leader could play to this horse's profile of running consistent figures without finding a decisive gear.

races.name: XIN GIN Irish EBF Brownstown Stakes (Fillies' & Mares' Group 3)

runners_data.name: Bella Isabella
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes partners a filly with a course-and-distance win to her name and strong similar-going form, but she races in the colours of a naturally prominent type who is liable to find her preferred pitch ahead of her in a field stacked with early movers — Weld's runner is at her best when on the pace, not behind it.

runners_data.name: Chantez
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll takes the ride for G M Lyons on a filly who has a useful 7f placing on Good ground in her recent lines; the headgear (blinkers) may sharpen her early effort, and she is the prominent runner most likely to actually secure a forward berth given Duckadilly's tendency to lead rather than press.

runners_data.name: Duckadilly
runners_data.note: The clear pace-setter on both style and form, she won last time over 8f on Good and steps back to her preferred 7f for Daniel McLoughlin; her only concern is a patchy overall form cycle (40-715), but with an uncontested lead on quick ground and a flat track, she is the race's dominant tactical asset.

runners_data.name: Fingerpaint
runners_data.note: Colin Keane rides a Weld-trained hold-up filly who won over this course and distance on Good ground and has the profile of a horse who can finish strongly with a clear run; the p headgear denotes hood, and her most recent run a month ago keeps her fresh — she is the most naturally suited closer in this field.

runners_data.name: Nancy J
runners_data.note: Ben Coen's mount for J P Murtagh carries the lowest OR in the field at 83 and her recent form string (583-04) is inconsistent, but she has course form at 7f on Good ground and the Murtagh yard has been in strong 14-day form (4/19); the concern is whether she can bridge the class gap from OR 83 against a field rated up to 17lbs superior.

runners_data.name: Phenomenal Filly
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners Paul Twomey's lightly-raced three-year-old whose last run was 285 days ago — a significant unknown — though she has a win at 7f on Good ground and her OR of 90 suggests talent; she carries the lightest weight at 127lbs and is a true prominent runner who will find her natural berth hard to secure with Duckadilly and Chantez ahead of her early.

races.paceDynamic: Duckadilly is the confirmed pace-setter here and, with no genuine rival pressing her for the lead, Scott McCullagh can dictate terms at a comfortable, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Leopardstown. Fingerpaint and Nancy J are the authentic hold-up runners and will track the pace from the rear, while Chantez can slot in behind Duckadilly at a natural prominent pitch. This field carries more prominent-running horses than the race shape can accommodate: Bella Isabella and Phenomenal Filly are both natural prominent types who will find the early positions congested, and one or both are likely to be shuffled back into a midfield role against their instincts. With Duckadilly setting a controlled, uncontested tempo, this race shape strongly favours a horse that can track the pace from second or third and produce a measured sustained finish — the lone genuine closer who gets a clean run at the leader on a flat track with two furlongs to run holds significant positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Duckadilly Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Duckadilly dictates an uncontested lead and the pace stays honest without acceleration
scenarios.body: Duckadilly settles in front with no one willing to press her hard, conserving enough energy through the final furlong on quick ground to hold the challenge; Colin Keane on Fingerpaint and Ben Coen on Nancy J will mount late runs but may be left with too much ground to make up if the front-runner doesn't fade

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Gets Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If Duckadilly's recent form dip (4-0-7-1-5 sequence) signals she cannot sustain a front-running effort over 7f on firm going
scenarios.body: Duckadilly sets a pace that flatters to deceive, and the stamina of the hold-up horses proves decisive inside the final furlong; Fingerpaint, whose last win came over 7f at Leopardstown in identical conditions, is ideally placed to pick up the pieces with Colin Keane using the flat track to maximum effect

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If one of the true prominent types — Bella Isabella or Chantez — manages to secure a forward position and produces a turn of foot off the pace
scenarios.body: Chantez has back-to-back placings at 7f on Good ground and Gary Carroll can slot her second or third behind Duckadilly, producing a challenge from a position of comfort; Bella Isabella's course form is strong but her redistribution to a deeper spot against her natural style reduces her effectiveness in a strongly-run finish

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Phenomenal Filly Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If the lightly-raced three-year-old Phenomenal Filly produces improvement after 285 days off and overcomes her positional disadvantage
scenarios.body: Having won over this exact 7f trip on Good ground, Paul Twomey's filly carries potential upside on form figures, but the lengthy absence and the fact she is unlikely to get her natural prominent pitch in a congested early shape make this a low-probability outcome dependent on raw class

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Bella Isabella or Phenomenal Filly can hold a prominent pitch at the start — if both are crowded back, the race shape becomes a clean lead-and-stay contest for Duckadilly with limited genuine pressure.

Duckadilly's form cycle (40-715) contains inconsistency despite the recent win; if Scott McCullagh cannot maintain her rhythm on the turn, the late runners Fingerpaint and Nancy J will close rapidly on the flat Leopardstown run-in.

Fingerpaint's headgear (hood) and hold-up style means Colin Keane will need a clear passage entering the final 2f — with six runners this is manageable, but any interference at that stage ends her chance immediately.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this race, matching the conditions in which Fingerpaint won and Duckadilly recorded her best form — no going concern for any runner, but the quick surface is likely to reward a horse with high cruising speed rather than a pure grinder.

Chantez has not run for 53 days and Gary Carroll will need to manage her freshness early — if the blinkers sharpen her too aggressively, she may over-race behind Duckadilly and fail to produce her finish in the closing stages.

races.name: Harry Meighan Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Glyndwr
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with two wins at the trip on Standard going, but only 0 wins and 2 places in 10 similar-going runs — needs a strong pace to cut back and may be flattered by a collapse in the lead.|

runners_data.name: Ocean Manifest
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner; wins at this trip on Standard, 111 days off, tongue-tie fitted, and a STYLE_FIT flag means racing slightly out of role here — dictates the tempo but must be marked down slightly for the layoff and the compressed role.|

runners_data.name: Bill Silvers
runners_data.note: 301 days absent is the single biggest red flag in the field; has placed at nine and ten furlongs on Soft but this drop in trip on Good to Firm comes cold after a long layoff, and the form line tails off sharply.|

runners_data.name: Dark Viper
runners_data.note: Prominent type who carries the best strike-rate in similar going (1W 4P from 9 runs), but OR=75 and a winless recent run of five suggest he finds one too good — should be competitive without necessarily getting to the front.|

runners_data.name: Heliogabalus
runners_data.note: Won at 8f Good twice recently and Colin Keane booked at OR=74 makes this one of the most potent jockey-form combinations in the race; proven prominent runner who should secure the second or third position behind Ocean Manifest with the best recent form in the field.|

runners_data.name: Dark Summit
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — nine of its last eleven runs on Good ground have resulted in finishes of eighth or worse; a hold-up type at OR=73 who gives little reason to expect improvement here.|

runners_data.name: Eddie G
runners_data.note: Has posted two places from five runs at seven to eight furlongs on Good — prominent type who has been competitive at this level without winning; tongue-tie worn, and jockey Adam Caffrey will need a clean break to secure a handy position.|

runners_data.name: Zaraahmando
runners_data.note: Trainer-jockey combo is the same person (Andrew Slattery), and this 4-year-old has a solid base of form at 8f on Good, with two wins from 15 similar-going runs — genuine prominent type who should find a slot behind the leader.|

runners_data.name: Frank Pickle
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose last five runs span ten to twelve furlongs — this step down to a mile on Good to Firm is a trip and going question, and the STYLE_FIT and redistribution flags mean Ben Coen is unlikely to get the position the horse wants.|

runners_data.name: Finsceal Annie
runners_data.note: Has one win and two places from fifteen similar-going attempts at this trip; tongue-tie and pads worn, and Dylan Browne McMonagle is the standout jockey booking — prominent type who may lack the finishing kick on this surface.|

runners_data.name: Hamiyan
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Dermot Weld's yard, 81 days off, with a hood fitted — has placed at 8f on Soft but only one run on Good going and a hold-up style means a lot depends on the pace being genuinely searching.|

runners_data.name: Liberate
runners_data.note: Consistent Good-ground performer at longer trips (ten to thirteen furlongs) who is compressed into a midfield slot; the hood is fitted and OR=66 means this is a horse finding its level, but the step down to a mile is a new question.|

runners_data.name: Ballymagreehan
runners_data.note: Won at 8f on Good last time and OR=64 is the lowest in the field — a naturally prominent type who has been remapped to midfield because of the crowded prominent group; Luke McAteer will struggle to get the position this horse needs.|

runners_data.name: Heart Of Eternity
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's third runner in the race at OR=62 with form of 14th, 14th, 8th at shorter trips — a true hold-up type mapped forward against its preference, and recent finishing positions give no encouragement at this level.|

races.paceDynamic: Ocean Manifest is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press from the outside, is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground around Leopardstown's flat mile. Heliogabalus, Dark Viper, Eddie G, Zaraahmando and Finsceal Annie all carry prominent tendencies but with Ocean Manifest already committed to the lead, several of these will be forced to slot in behind rather than stride alongside — the pace will be real but not truly contested. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can all get their natural position: among the prominent runners, Heliogabalus and Zaraahmando are most likely to secure the seats directly behind Ocean Manifest, while Ballymagreehan, Frank Pickle, Liberate and Heart Of Eternity — though natural hold-up or prominent types — are redistributed rearward and their true tactical preferences will be compromised. A single, unflustered pace-setter on a flat track with a good surface sets up a race that will be run at an honest but not frantic tempo, with the finish likely coming down to who can sustain their run from the two-furlong pole — this shape strongly favours on-pace horses with a proven turn of foot on Good or faster ground who can sit close without being crowded out early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, On-Pace Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ocean Manifest bowls along uncontested and the race is run at an honest but unspectacular tempo, rewarding horses who can sit second or third and quicken from two out.
scenarios.body: Ocean Manifest sets a solo lead with Heliogabalus and Zaraahmando tucked in close, and the race is effectively over when the kick comes in the final two furlongs on the fast surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Ocean Manifest goes too fast in front and the gallop burns itself out, opening the door for horses held up to come from further back.
scenarios.body: The lead softens past two furlongs out and runners held off a strong pace find the track opening up in the final furlong on the quick ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Scrappy Pace, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early positioning proves messy with several prominent types jostling for spots, producing an uneven gallop that suits a mid-to-late mover.
scenarios.body: The fractured early pace creates a bunched mid-race scenario and a horse who threads through smoothly from mid-pack lands the spoils.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sticks
scenarios.trigger: If Ocean Manifest is allowed to dictate entirely on its own terms and the prominent pack fails to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: With no one willing or able to go with Ocean Manifest, the leader controls every fraction and simply outstays a field that has left too much to do.

watchPoints.text: Ocean Manifest has been off 111 days, carries a tongue-tie, and is the lone pace-setter — any sign of rustiness or reluctance to load cleanly could collapse the whole pace structure and hand the race to closers immediately.

Heliogabalus and Zaraahmando both want to race prominently and could physically collide for the same ground directly behind Ocean Manifest in the early stages — monitor the draw and how cleanly each breaks.

Ballymagreehan, Frank Pickle, Liberate and Heart Of Eternity are all tagged redistributed — if any of them manage to push forward and create a contested early pace, the controlled scenario unravels and the tempo quickens sharply.

Good to Firm is the confirmed going for this race despite the card listing Good — horses with CONCERN flags on fast ground should be reassessed, and the quick surface will particularly test Bill Silvers returning from 301 days off.
Denis Hogan saddles three runners (Dark Summit, Liberate, Heart Of Eternity) — watch for market moves on any of the three as a yard signal, particularly if one drifts and another shortens late.

races.name: Double First Stables Irish EBF Nasrullah Handicap (Premier Handicap)

runners_data.name: Diego El Queso
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter for Lyons/Keane, but his form at 9f on similar ground reads 4 runs, no wins — the step up in trip and lone-leader role suits tactically, though his OR of 97 and 85 days off means fitness is a mild query; style fit tag notes he is mapping slightly out of role as a prominent type forced to lead.

runners_data.name: Lord Massusus
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a plodding recent form string (8-6-3-6-8) and no wins from 15 runs on good ground — apprentice jockey Sam Coen (5lb claim) adds interest but the 11-day turnaround and lack of recent improvement make him hard to trust even in a pace-dependent scenario.

runners_data.name: Cloud Seeker
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery, which is a notable dual role angle; prominent runner with strong good-ground stats (3W6P from 13 runs), though his last three runs were over longer trips (9-12f) and the drop to 9f may sharpen him up rather than stretch him.

runners_data.name: Retracement
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has won on good ground over 10f for Murtagh — the step down from 10-12f trips to 9f is a query on stamina grounds, but his OR drop to 87 means he is well handicapped if the trip suits; Ben Coen retains the ride and he maps as a genuine prominent type.

runners_data.name: Slieve Binnian
runners_data.note: Marnane's older horse has a naturally prominent style but this field is too deep in pace for him to replicate that position — his last five runs show a pattern of fading in the final stages (9-6-10-13-5) and the redistribution to midfield mirrors what will likely happen on the track.

runners_data.name: Playin Cool
runners_data.note: Won over 9f on heavy but his only two good-ground runs produced a 3rd and a 15th — the going switch is a real concern, and being a naturally prominent horse who won't get to the front in this field means he is racing against his grain on a surface that already clouds his chance.

runners_data.name: Jamestown
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a tidy recent profile (4-2-2-1-3) for Marnane, strong on good and soft, and tactically well placed as a genuine prominent runner who should secure a handy position without a fight — the step up from 7-8f to 9f looks an asset and Luke McAteer is a capable jockey in a Premier Handicap.

runners_data.name: Harana
runners_data.note: Just won over 10f on good ground for Weld, fits the up-in-class narrative well, and wears a hood — naturally forward-going but the volume of pace in this field means she is likely to sit closer to midfield than her instincts suggest; the 17-day turnaround is fine and her form over this type of going is solid.

runners_data.name: Nakasero
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who wears a tongue-tie and has been running over 10-12f in Ireland — the drop back to 9f is speculative, and his natural prominent style will be squeezed back by the cluster of similar types; De Bromhead's yard is at 5/45 in the last 14 days and the 55-day absence adds another layer of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Thread Of Gold
runners_data.note: Mullins three-year-old with a compact but promising form line (1-7-3 from three runs), all on good ground — the step up to 9f looks logical and Wayne Lordan's booking is significant; 39 days since last run is not unusual for this yard and his profile as a lightly raced improver makes him one of the most interesting in the field.

runners_data.name: Harmani
runners_data.note: Lyons three-year-old in form (won over 10f, placed twice recently) — naturally a front-going type who will be squeezed back by the weight of pace, but Rory Mulligan's 5lb claim keeps the weight competitive; his good-ground form is limited (2/6 runs) but his recent trajectory is upward.

runners_data.name: Anvika
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a consistent placed record on soft (3-3) but struggles on good (10th, 8th) — the going report confirming Good to Firm is a genuine concern, and her OR of 73 means she is carrying least weight but is significantly outclassed at this level even in a pace-collapse scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Diego El Queso is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m1f. The absence of serious pace pressure means the tempo is unlikely to be brutal, creating a race that will unfold in a relatively strung-out fashion with the leader dictating terms into the straight. Prominent racers who can travel just off the pace — Jamestown, Cloud Seeker, and Thread Of Gold — are best placed to exploit this shape, as the compressed gallop into the home turn suits those with a handy position and a turn of foot rather than those relying on a searching pace to set up a late run. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Harmani, Slieve Binnian, Playin Cool, Harana, and Nakasero are all genuine prominent horses remapped to midfield — of those, Harmani (consistent recent form, Lyons yard) and Harana (just won) are most likely to actually push forward and recover some ground, but the true beneficiaries of this shape are the legitimate prominent runners who get there without a fight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Diego El Queso dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the race is won by a prominent racer tracking just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Diego El Queso rolls along in front without being pressured, setting a fair but manageable tempo that keeps the field strung out and rewards those travelling smoothly in second or third; Jamestown and Thread Of Gold are ideally suited, both carrying the right profile and strong recent form to pick up through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Lasts, Pressers Punished
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that Diego El Queso's stamina reserves go untested and he kicks clear from the front in the straight.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow early gallop gifts the leader an unchallenged advantage and the lack of real pressure means prominent challengers never quite close the gap; those tracking in second and third are caught flat-footed when the leader quickens, favouring the horse with the best finishing kick among the prominents.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Get Gap
scenarios.trigger: If a moderate tempo bunches the field, creating a scrimmage in the straight that opens late ground for redistributed horses who find room.
scenarios.body: The compressed race shape produces a messy home straight with horses fanning wide, giving horses like Harmani and Harana — both naturally prominent but mapped back — the chance to exploit gaps if they get a clear run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the held-up runners Lord Massusus and Anvika finish with real momentum.
scenarios.body: Only in a scenario where Diego El Queso sets a genuinely fast pace do the true hold-up horses Lord Massusus and Anvika get a meaningful late run; Lord Massusus has done it on good ground before but his recent form string is unconvincing and Anvika is significantly outrated, making this the least-likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Jamestown is the horse to watch for position in the first furlong — if Luke McAteer gets him travelling smoothly just off Diego El Queso's flank, he ticks every box this race shape is likely to reward.
Thread Of Gold's Mullins booking and unexposed profile make him dangerous if Lordan opts to track the pace prominently from the outset rather than dropping him in.

Harmani, Slieve Binnian, Playin Cool, Harana, and Nakasero will all be jostling for prominent ground in the first two furlongs — watch for shuffling, crowding, and any of these being checked or forced wide early, which will neutralise their chances entirely.

Diego El Queso has not won in four runs at this distance on similar ground — if he ties up in the final furlong rather than kicking clear, the prominent runners behind him could swamp him in a tight finish.

Cloud Seeker's trainer-ridden angle is worth monitoring in the betting — any significant market move given the dual Slattery role would be meaningful context for how confident connections are on this drop in trip.

races.name: Mervue Equine Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Burford Beauty
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Gavin Cromwell and Gary Carroll, handles good ground well with two placed efforts in similar conditions, steps up from 7-8f and the extra distance here looks a positive angle.

runners_data.name: Mullacurry Maid
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up racer whose sole comparable going run produced only 5th, limited placed form (0W0P), and the fades-in-finish flag raises serious doubts in a 25-runner race where getting a clear passage late is already difficult.

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes a prominent booking on this hold-up type who actually has two places on good ground in his last 15 starts; the fades-in-finish flag and the step back in trip from staying distances are concerns despite the high-profile rider.

runners_data.name: Anchors Away
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for M G Quinn ridden by apprentice Paddy Harnett, has placed at 10f on good and good-to-soft but carries the fades-in-finish flag and has failed to win from 8 comparable-going starts.

runners_data.name: Max Meridius
runners_data.note: Deep hold-up performer who has spent most of his career over 16f-plus trips; dropping sharply in distance to 9f is a bold move and his good-ground form over staying trips offers limited guide to what he produces here.

runners_data.name: Medieval Night
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with blinkers and a tongue-tie, has two places on good ground but the fades-in-finish concern is significant in a big field where he will need to weave through traffic from the rear.

runners_data.name: Not Simple
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for James Barrett with Gavin Ryan up, has been absent 51 days and all his comparable-going form comes at 7-8f on heavy or soft surfaces — the switch to good-to-firm is a genuine question mark.

runners_data.name: Slaney Swagger
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for amateur Nicola Burns who has five places in similar conditions without winning, handles 8f on good ground and is on a reasonable surface, though 25 runners and a moderate pace are not ideal for a pure closer.

runners_data.name: Shelbourne Flyer
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride on this natural hold-up horse who holds good-ground form at 7f; genuinely placed back from the rear because the field is packed with closers, so Keane will likely push him to a more prominent position than his style suggests — style-fit discount applies.

runners_data.name: Nibras Rainbow
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, handled in Paul Flynn's yard alongside stable companions; his last win came over 8f on good ground and he drops to a manageable mark of OR52 — the uncontested lead is his primary asset and he carries a minor style-fit note as he races more prominently than his mapped position implies.

runners_data.name: Shahada Ace
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery, this hold-up type has one win from 13 comparable-going starts but the fades-in-finish flag and the redistribution from his natural rearward position into the midfield map mean his chance is materially harder to execute than his form suggests.

runners_data.name: Sayfa Fad
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse from the Paul Flynn yard who won over 8f on good ground at OR that makes this competitive; he is mapped to midfield because the field is too close-heavy, so securing his natural late-run position is genuinely problematic — style-fit caution warranted.

runners_data.name: Alto Sax
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this hold-up type who actually won over 10f on good ground 27 days ago — the most recent winning form in the field; shown in midfield due to the over-supply of closers, but Coen's positional skills could help him find a better spot than his natural style allows.

runners_data.name: Yquem
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes on a hold-up type who won over 9f on good ground 21 days ago, giving him a recent winning profile on the right surface; the redistribution into midfield from the rear means he is in a slightly better map position than his natural running style and could be a live danger if things go his way.

runners_data.name: Morning Approach
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up horse for McCreery and W J Lee, absent 27 days, all recent good-ground runs have produced mid-to-rear finishes at 8f, and the fades-in-finish flag in a field of 25 makes a winning effort very hard to construct.

runners_data.name: Famous Enough
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for Patrick Foley — one of only two genuine pace horses in the race; has a win on similar ground at 8f and two places in comparable conditions, and his natural position just off Nibras Rainbow gives him a real tactical advantage in this shape.

runners_data.name: Folk Warrior
runners_data.note: Hold-up type stepping down from staying trips of 12-16f; his best form on good ground came over 10f, so the 9f trip is a slight question, and the redistribution from the rear means he won't get his preferred position in this size of field.

runners_data.name: La Campanella
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Gerard Keane who fades in finishes and whose only good-ground form at relevant distances produced two 4ths from 9 starts; racing out of natural position in a 25-runner field is a compounding difficulty.

runners_data.name: Lady Crossing
runners_data.note: Apprentice Jack Cleary rides this fading hold-up type who is mapped away from her natural rearward position; best effort on comparable ground was a 4th over 8f on soft, and the step up to 9f with a style-fit concern makes this look tough.

runners_data.name: Milverton
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type for Karl Thornton with tongue-tie and blinkers, raced 8 days ago, has placed once from 15 comparable-going runs; the genuine midfield map position is marginally better than his usual rear slot but his overall profile is moderate.

runners_data.name: Quarry Stone
runners_data.note: A two-year-old on a 273-day break, form figures show double-figure finishes in most recent comparable runs, and racing into a 25-runner handicap off a long absence is a severe ask regardless of pace shape.

runners_data.name: Half Nutz
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type for James Barcoe who has shown commendable consistency with two places in the last six on good ground; his redistribution into midfield from his natural rear position is only a partial benefit, but E E Ryan's experience could help him find the clearest route through.

runners_data.name: Rushford
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Thomas Hughes who carries the fades-in-finish flag across all recent runs; form figures of 9/0/9/0/9 on comparable ground speak clearly, and the 8-day turnaround adds little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Jazz Dreamers
runners_data.note: Absent 160 days, hold-up type whose best comparable-ground run produced 7th; the long layoff combined with the fades-in-finish concern and a redistribution away from his natural position make this a very difficult puzzle to solve.

runners_data.name: Master Garvey
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Joseph Murray with apprentice Wesley Joyce, has placed once from 15 comparable-going runs; recent 7th over 10f on good ground is the most relevant piece of form but does not suggest he is dangerous in this company.

races.paceDynamic: Nibras Rainbow is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 25-horse field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to press or challenge him through the early stages, meaning he can control tempo entirely on his own terms over this flat 1m1f at Leopardstown on good-to-firm ground. With no one likely to chase him hard, he can bowl along at a sustainable, even gallop — the kind that keeps the field strung out but doesn't produce the stop-start fractions that would bring closers flying home. Famous Enough is the only other prominent-style runner likely to sit close to the pace alongside or just off Nibras Rainbow, giving the front end a small but real presence. The field holds substantially more hold-up and deep-closing types than the map can physically place at the rear — Shelbourne Flyer, Shahada Ace, Sayfa Fad, Alto Sax, Yquem, and Morning Approach are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield slots, meaning true rearward racing will be even more crowded than it appears. This controlled, uncontested pace on a flat course strongly favours horses who travel prominently or just off the pace, as the gallop will be honest enough to stretch the field but the finish line will arrive before closers from far back can fully close down a front-runner who has conserved energy throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nibras Rainbow Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Nibras Rainbow dictates a smooth, uncontested lead and the tempo stays measured enough that he retains his momentum into the straight.
scenarios.body: Leigh Roche will find no reason to push for early position with zero pace rivals, allowing Nibras Rainbow to coast along and produce a strong, sustained finish on good-to-firm ground that suits him; horses sitting prominently just off him, like Famous Enough, will be best placed to challenge if he ties up late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Draw Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Nibras Rainbow and Famous Enough both stride into the straight with daylight in hand and the hold-up pack fails to reel them in from the rear.
scenarios.body: The steady pace benefits the two horses at the front of the race who have tracked the tempo throughout rather than expending energy weaving through 25 runners in the straight; the redistributed closers, forced wider and further back than their natural position, simply run out of ground on the flat Leopardstown layout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is set just fast enough that Nibras Rainbow tightens up near home and a well-positioned midfield or hold-up runner picks up the pieces in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse like Alto Sax or Yquem, both possessing recent winning form on good ground and sitting nearer the actual midfield than their natural rear position would suggest, could benefit if there is enough tempo late to reward the sustained run; this scenario is discounted because the majority of genuine closers are redistributed and will be further back than the scenario requires.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Chaos, Backmarker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the field of 25 causes significant traffic problems mid-race, the pace fragments, and a freshly dropped-in backmarker threads through on the best ground.
scenarios.body: With 25 runners on a flat track, interference and crowding are possible even at a calm pace, and a horse who finds a clear run late — such as Half Nutz or Shelbourne Flyer, who both have good-ground form and a recent win in their profiles — could steal the frame in a messy finish; this is the lowest-probability shape because the uncontested pace makes fragmentation unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Nibras Rainbow's early stride pattern is the race key — watch whether Leigh Roche lets him bowl along unchallenged or is forced to check; if he settles in an uncontested rhythm he holds a significant positional edge over all 24 rivals.

Famous Enough is the only horse with a genuine claim to sit close to the pace in second or third position — if Luke McAteer secures that slot early, watch him come into the frame as the field straightens for home with cover used.

The redistribution cluster of Alto Sax, Yquem, Shelbourne Flyer, and Sayfa Fad will all be jostling for positions that don't naturally belong to them; watch for crowding and shuffling on the turn into the straight as 25 horses compress through the flat Leopardstown bend.

races.name: Hurling For Cancer Research Supported By Centra On July 24th (Q.R.) Race

runners_data.name: Delta
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's four-year-old holds form over comparable trips on good ground (1W3P in similar conditions) and arrives fresh on 13 days' rest with Mr P W Mullins in the plate — the sole genuine hold-up horse in the race, she needs the pace to be honest enough to reel rivals in from off the bridle.

runners_data.name: The Mediator
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's nine-year-old has winning form on soft and recorded three places recently, including a third at 14f on good — a naturally prominent-going type who is squeezed out of that position here by the preponderance of forward-running rivals and will find himself racing further back than he would like.

runners_data.name: Sirius
runners_data.note: W P Mullins sends out this seven-year-old returning after a 261-day absence, with a mixed profile on similar ground (1W1P in 11 runs) and a history that includes front-running wins — though his natural desire to race prominently cannot be accommodated in this field and he is unlikely to get anywhere near his preferred pitch.

runners_data.name: Catalani
runners_data.note: The class act in the field on OR=120 with an amateur rider, Jack Foley's seven-year-old has winning and placed form over marathon trips on good ground (1W2P in similar conditions in 3 of 4 runs) — well-suited by the stamina test and, as a prominent type with fewer rivals ahead of him than the field-shape suggests, is the most likely horse to actually secure a position close to Murat.

runners_data.name: Friary Road
runners_data.note: T M Walsh's six-year-old has been absent for 336 days (70 jumping days), carrying 156lbs for an amateur; prior form includes a win at 16f on good, but this is a horse who wants to race forward — with three other prominent-minded runners ahead of him in the queue, getting into a comfortable rhythm from a position he enjoys will be far from straightforward.

runners_data.name: Murat
runners_data.note: Peter Lawlor's confirmed front-runner arrives on 19 days' rest with OR=120 and Mr H C Swan up — holds good-ground form (3W3P in 7 runs, including a Leopardstown win at 16f) and is set to dictate in a race with no natural rival to press him; the STYLE_FIT flag reminds that conditions could yet test his stamina if he over-exerts early.

races.paceDynamic: Murat is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing to press him from the outset, he is set to control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 1m7f trip on good-to-firm ground at Leopardstown. The absence of any meaningful pace pressure means he can dictate every fraction, conserve energy through the middle portion of the race, and force rivals to come to him — a classic recipe for the leader to last home. Delta, the lone genuine hold-up horse, will be the main beneficiary of any pace collapse, needing the fractions to be honest enough to close into, but a slow-run race risks stranding her. This race shape strongly favours Murat's front-running profile and any close tracker who is tactically versatile enough to sit within striking range — the field contains more prominent-minded horses than can realistically secure their natural position, with Catalani best-placed among the nominally prominent types to actually get close to the pace given class and course foothold, while Sirius, The Mediator, and Friary Road are all true prominent racers who are unlikely to slot into their preferred spot and are mapped to midfield as a result.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Murat Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Murat leads without serious pressure and sets a pace he fully controls from the first to the last furlong.
scenarios.body: Murat dictates a measured tempo, making every yard of the running and conserving enough for a punishing last two furlongs on the fast ground — rivals arriving from behind face a wall of front-running stubbornness. Horses who can sit close without overdoing it in the early stages are ideally positioned to capitalise if he tires, but the greater likelihood is he simply holds on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Trackers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly too strong and Murat begins to tire inside the final two furlongs, allowing a close-tracking rival to pick him off.
scenarios.body: Catalani, able to sit just off Murat's shoulder given class and experience over stamina trips, would be the prime beneficiary as the early pace proves just a fraction too hot to sustain into the straight. Delta, coming from further back, could also close strongly if the fractions were genuinely searching.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If Murat and any tracking rivals have overdone it sufficiently to leave the race wide open for a sweeping late challenge from the rear.
scenarios.body: Delta has the form at similar trips on good ground and Mr P W Mullins in the saddle adds tactical nous for a patient hold-up ride — a genuinely strong pace would be needed to bring this scenario to life. Without that honest gallop, however, Delta's closing run risks arriving too late against a front-runner who was never seriously threatened.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Race Shape
scenarios.trigger: If a wayward pace, jostling for position among the redistributed prominent types, or a messy start scrambles the expected running order entirely.
scenarios.body: If the natural prominent runners — Sirius, The Mediator, and Friary Road — all push forward despite the mapping, a contested early pace could unravel Murat's control and open the race unpredictably. Any horse with stamina in reserve and tactical flexibility benefits, but this remains the least probable outcome given the small field size and Murat's established front-running pattern.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Sirius, The Mediator, or Friary Road push hard for position in the opening furlongs — if two or more of these displaced prominent types contest the early lead, Murat's pace control is broken and the entire race shape changes.

Catalani is returning from a 66-day absence under an amateur rider (Mr B T Stone, 7lb claimer) at OR=120 — if he is short of peak fitness or the jockey is overcautious, his ability to sit close enough to Murat to matter in the straight is compromised.

Murat's STYLE_FIT flag at 0.91 is a reminder that, despite confirmed front-running habits, his form in good-ground conditions is narrower than headline figures suggest — monitor whether he is strongly pressed at any stage, as even minimal pressure could shorten his stamina reserves over 1m7f.

Delta's chance is entirely conditional on pace: if Murat is allowed a slow or moderate gallop, the closing ground for a hold-up horse simply will not materialise over this distance — watch the early splits to judge whether her run is live before the home turn.
